Gotta love a Monday muffin bake. Actually my intention for baking today was to have some fresh muffins for after the kids swim session tonight as a little treat. But the leftovers will get stored in fridge and freezer for future bites.

They are also extremely nutrient dense with butter, eggs, milk & yogurt. My kids don’t always eat these in isolation but wrapped up in a muffin, a win!

In these yummy muffins here’s what we’ve got

1 3/4 cup spelt flour
1 tsp baking soda
1 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon 
1/2 tsp sea salt
1/2 cup melted butter
1/2 cup coconut sugar
1-2 ripened bananas
2 large eggs
1/4 cup milk
1 tbsp yogurt

So with @hukitchen gems and some with fresh blueberries 🩵

Preheat oven to 425°F and line with muffin liners.
In a large bowl, whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together until combined. Set aside.
In a medium bowl, whisk the butter, coconut sugar, bananas, eggs, and milk together until combined. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, and then fold everything together gently just until combined and no flour pockets remain.
Spoon the batter into liners, filling them all the way to the top.
Bake for 5 minutes at 425°F, then, keeping the muffins in the oven, reduce the oven temperature to 350°F (177°C). Bake for an additional 16–17 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. The total time these muffins take in the oven is about 21–22 minutes, give or take. Allow the muffins to cool for 5 minutes in the muffin pan before enjoying. 
Cover tightly and store at room temperature for up to 1 week.

caption:
You are going to want to save this one!!
I love making meatloaf, but the last few times I’ve made it, it’s been on the dry side. Since my Dutch oven has become my new bff & keeps everything moist, I figured this had to work. Luckily it turned out better than I could have imagined & the whole family loved it.

Here’s what I did :) 

What you need:
1/2 cup chopped onion
2 eggs 
1/4 cup bone broth
1/2 cup almond flour or breadcrumbs 
1/2 cup natural ketchup (I like @primalkitchenfoods)
1 tsp Italian seasoning
1 tsp dried parsley
1 tsp salt
2 lbs ground organic beef

For the glaze/sauce 
1/2 up ketchup
2 tsp coconut sugar
1 tsp coconut aminos
2 tbsp dijon mustard

* Preheat your oven to 300°F.
* In a large mixing bowl, combine all the meatloaf ingredients except the ground beef.
* Add the ground beef to the mixture and gently mix until just combined—avoid overmixing for the best texture.
* Shape the mixture into a loaf and carefully place it in the bottom of your Dutch oven and cover with glaze. Pour some extra bone broth around meat at bottom of pot approximately 1/2 cup.
* Let it sit for 20-30 minutes.
* Bake for 2 hours covered at 300 and you should have a perfect meatloaf!

Serve with bone broth and olive oil infused mashed potatoes and steamed green beans! Makes excellent leftovers.

I won Sarelle over with the meat & Hayden with the potatoes 🫠

Enjoy for your next family dinner.

Although I am birthing a new part of me, it is really just an extension. I am taking all my years of knowledge & experience and niche it into the area that I am now most excited about, mom and baby nutrition.

Pregnancy can be such an exciting time, but it can also be a time full of unknowns and uncertainty. You have many decisions to make over the course of your pregnancy. While you’re picking out baby names and organizing baby clothes, it’s important to make your nutrition a priority as well.

Proper nutrition is essential for both you and your baby, but figuring out what to eat during pregnancy can be very confusing. The nutrients that are supplied to your baby must come from the foods you eat, otherwise, they will be taken from your own body. This depletion of your reserves can have many unfortunate consequences on your own health. 

With the support of a Certified Nutrition Consultant, it’s possible to reduce your chances of “morning” sickness (more appropriately: all day, any time nausea!), fatigue, constipation, heartburn, mood swings, pre-eclampsia, anemia, gestational diabetes, postpartum depression, and more.

Nourishing your pregnancy will help your baby build solid bones, a strong immunity, healthy tissue and organs. It’s also possible to reduce their risk of birth defects, low birth weight, allergies, conditions such as eczema or asthma, and many potential health problems later in life.
Providing your body with the proper nutrition will help provide your baby with the best start possible.

Nutrition consulting will empower you with the knowledge and confidence that you are doing the best for your baby and your body.

caption:
There is hope!

I am so thrilled that eggs are now included again as Sarelle’s “yes” foods!
I thought she would never eat eggs again after they were such a staple from 6 -18 months. Then just like that, they were gone.
But here we are making scrambled eggs. She sees me and Hayden eat them all the time and she finally asked for her own portion a few weeks ago. 

Actually, I think it went something along the lines of this:
Me: Do you want eggs today for lunch? (jokingly knowing there is no chance)
S: Yes! 
Me: Really? Like really?
S: Yes, but only scrambled not hard boiled or any other way.
Me: (I didn’t say anything, I just happily complied with a little happy dance!)

I’m so happy as eggs are one of the most nutritious foods that she could eat. If I could have picked one food I wish she was eating again, this would have been it! Somedays I feel so out of options for breakfast especially. But today, scrambled eggs it was! I realize she may not want them all the time, but at least they are an option.

If your child has refused certain foods they ate as a baby, don’t give up. You may have to for a bit after you keep trying over and over… But eventually they may come around on their own time.

It’s so hard not to keep pushing the foods you want them to eat, I admit, I am guilty of this. But I am learning to just lean back and they will come to you.

#dontgiveup #feedingkids #thereshope #eggs

Wearing our true food philosophy while also engaging in all the fun 🍳🥓

There’s no doubt Halloween is an interesting time for all parents navigating the highs and lows of sugar/goodie intake.

We love the spirit and fun of the night and seeing our kids excitement is everything. However the allure of candy is real especially as my kids get older and they want to be part of the fun and we want them to as well.

Last night we went out with friends, gathered candy and then came home to oodles of “other” treats some homemade some store bought and let them go to town while they exchanged their bags. They were just as excited about the other healthier options as their bag of treats.

That doesn’t mean I won’t let my kids try regular treats to experience them for themselves and how their body responds. It’s not easy, but it’s important 🤎

I don’t have all the answers yet of how this will pan out in the long term, but last night was amazing and my goal is to raise intuitive eaters that can find balance when it comes to food. My job is to provide the knowledge at home and their job is to take it into the world and experience it for themselves 💛

I love a good soup! So I’m not quite sure why I haven’t been making them that often 🤔

This week I was going through my pantry trying to use up my pulses and legumes, and these yellow split peas were calling me to be cooked up.

So I soaked 2 cups them for about an hour.

Sautéed up a half of white onion, 2 garlic cloves, 2 carrots chopped and celery.
Added in some sea salt, dried thyme & parsley.
Added in my soaked peas and poured in about 2 cups of homemade chicken bone broth and let it all simmer for about 20 minutes. Then added another 2 cups of filtered water and simmered for an additional 40. More water or broth can be added to thin it out.

It can also be blended, but I like it chunky 💛

Enjoy!

#soupseason #soupson #yellowsplitpea

1 small white onions 🧅

2 carrots chopped 🥕 
2-4 stalks of celery chopped
2 cups bone broth
2 cups water
1/2 tsp of cumin
1/4 tsp turmeric

1/4 tsp ginger powder

Sautée the veggies & garlic in 1-2 tbsp olive oil until tender. Add in bone broth, water and lentils. Bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes and add in your spices.

Most kids are afraid to ride a bike without training wheels and that is for a very good reason, they don’t learn how to balance properly.

Let’s make homemade granola!

So easy, so clean and you’ll be happy to have it on hand. Feel free to make it grain-free by omitting the oats and upping the nut ratios.

4 cups rolled oats
1/2 cup chopped pecans
1/2 cup chopped cashews
1/2 cup chopped walnuts
1 cup shredded coconut
1/4 cup maple syrup
1/2 cup coconut oil
1 tsp cinnamon
Pinch of sea salt

Mix it all up in a large bowl. Spread on a baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes at 250 and then toss and bake again for another 15 minutes until golden brown. 

Let it cool and store in a large airtight jar! If you are lucky it will last longer than a week 🙈

caption:
The most precious (and often very challenging) moments of the last 3.5 years have been spent nursing my little ones. 
Challenges have come and gone in physical and emotional ways.

But knowing that I was able to grow, nurture, protect and soothe my kids with my breasts and the milk that they made (and still make) is so incredible.

I will cherish my time with Hayden as he continues to nurse at 21 months (my boob man 🤍)

I have also recently accepted the new phase I in with Sarelle since she weaned in the last few months. She weaned herself for those asking…

I didn’t know how it was going to go down but it was perfect just the way it was. I don’t even necessarily know when our last session was but I know our 3 + year journey was so special.

There is no right or wrong length of time to breastfeed for, whatever feels right for you.

So on the last day of August, #nationalbreastfeedingmonth I am capturing three of many special moments with my babes. The second and last picture both Sarelle and Hayden were 20 months old 🤎

#breastfeedingmom #nursingmama #momsmilk #breastfed #worldbreastfeedingweek #bonding
